Measuring atomic disorder levels is vital for understanding how changes in local structural environments influence material performance and longevity. This study utilizes graph neural networks to establish a physically interpretable index for local disorder. This index characterizes the variety of immediate atomic arrangements as a smooth continuum ranging from solid to liquid states, deviating from traditional, bimodal "solid vs. liquid" classifactions. Specifically, we evaluate ice surfaces by categorizing atoms as disordered or ordered relative to an underlying lattice structure. By integrating these spatial patterns, we demonstrate that our model captures evolving degrees of thermal expansion across the interface. These observed variations align with changes in atomic-scale randomness, confirming that our method offers a accessible framework for quantifying thermally induced structural trends. Ultimately, this approach enables the mapping of subtle, continuous shifts in a two-state system, illustrating how incremental increases in microstructural randomness drive macroscopic physical properties.

Given a parametric family $f(y;\theta)$ for $y \in Y$ with $\theta \in \Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, let $P(Y=y_i|\theta)=f(y_i;\theta)$ represent independent observations $y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$ generated from a unknown mixture distribution $g(y|\varphi))=\int_Y g(y|t)\cdot h(y|\varphi)) \,dy)$. The objective is to construct an estimator $\hat{\theta}$ for $\varphi$. Estimators $\hat{\theta}_G$ and $\hat{\theta}_{ML}$ are identified through the generalized maximum likelihood (GML) method and conventional maximum likelihood estimation respectively. Key properties of these estimators, the conditions ensuring their strong and weak consistency, and an influence function analysis are provided specifically for the GML case $\hat{\theta}_G$. In the context of survey sampling, if $y_i$ corresponds to response data from unit $i$ out of a sample, then $h(y_i|\varphi)$ acts as the sampling weight; thus, the proposed methodology effectively estimates mean values for both population parameters using sampled information.

Knowledge Tracing (KT) applies students' historical interaction records to model their evolving knowledge states and predict their future learning outcomes. While deep learning-based approaches for KT have recently achieved significant advancements, the exact drivers behind these DL-KT models remain elusive, and their proper evaluation and analysis continue to be difficult tasks. Specifically, existing methods typically rely on proprietary and custom data cleaning workflows, impeding experimental standardization. Moreover, these studies often utilize varying protocols that fail to reflect genuine educational environments. To resolve these issues, we present *\textsc{pyKT}*, a robust Python-driven framework designed to facilitate knowledge tracing research. \textsc{pyKT} integrates standardized, clean datasets along with diverse deep learning-based KT models. This library not only unifies the benchmarking process using a single dataset but also offers various assessment dimensions, including multiple dataset partitions, distinct student selection strategies, and both aggregate and granular performance metrics. \textsc{pyKT} is distinguished by its capacity to conduct meticulous analyses of DL-KT approaches; consequently, it unifies the most current dimensional analysis frameworks such as Difficulty Analysis, Novelty Analysis, and Representativeness Analysis into the single library. Using \textsc{pyKT}, our investigation reveals that current DL-KT models require further refinement, particularly regarding their adherence to standardized educational principles, positioning the library as a complete tool for calibrating DL-KT models based on these real-world educational constraints.

This work demonstrates that a second-order elliptic differential operator $P$ possesses a closed range within the smooth function space $C^\infty(M)$ on any manifold $M$. Moreover, for any manifold $M$ lacking compact subcomponents, $P$ demonstrates surjectivity on $C^\infty(M)$, with this result having the potential to serve a foundational role in other investigations.

The version of the proof format adopted by the veriT SMT solver was initially showcased ten years ago following the first PxTP workshop. Since its inception, this format has fully evolved to the point where it supports various SMT applications, with other proof-producing solvers also generating files in this format. To secure a better direction for future advancements in this format, this article aims to solicit input from practitioners. To achieve that, it will examine the evolution history of the format as well as the pragmatic strategies used through its development while discussing the issues that may arise when other generating-proofs engines rely on the veriT proofs format.

Synchronous updates often reduce efficiency in cross-device federated learning, specifically as the pool of active clients expands. Nguyen et al., 2022 demonstrated with their approach, dubbed FedBuff, that incorporating asynchronous updates—including some degree of staleness—can resolve this issue. By adopting this method to scale training more effectively, the algorithm ensures privacy remains intact. In revisiting and extending this algorithm for use with the other asynchronous federated computations considered earlier, we also lift the standard assumptions on the bounded norm of gradient updates. Finally, the current work provides a thorough analysis of this adjusted approach in conditions characterized both in its training performance with delayed and stochastic data updates as in its non-stationarity risks.

Recent advance in neural end-to-end Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has led to optimal performance outcomes, however their effective deployment depends on access to vast datasets and significant computational power transfer-learning strategies have evolved; to address this constraint, even across related language boundaries, for instance, using an English-driven system to train for the German ASR language. However, this research examines more linguistically distant languages and reuse the same English model to train for the Czech language. The authors then proposed a simplified transfer-learning approach using the intermediate no-accent Czech character set; using this technique improved the model by reducing training times while also improving final results for the Czech model.

We introduce a Temporal Difference (TD) learning approach designed to tackle the navigation challenges marine robots encounter in underwater settings. To enhance data efficiency and ensure compatibility with real-time operations, the method integrates Gaussian Process regression with an advanced rejection-sparing algorithm. This framework derives the predictive distribution for the state value and utilizes these moments to propose SPGP-SARSA, novel algorithm for model-free policy evaluation. SPGP-TD emerges from straightforward modifications to SPGP-SARSA, establishing a corresponding model-based variant. Both algorithms are validated via extensive simulations as well as practical tests using a submersible, where SPGP variants demonstrate clear superiority over current state-of-the-art techniques across three distinct scenarios: value mapping that outperforms competing methods, data efficiency exceeded by a factor of 2 to 6, and computational latency satisfactory for live robotic applications.

We use a general, covariant interpretation (1+1+2 semi-tetrad approach) of a perfectly static stellar object with spherical symmetry, composed of anisotropy and two fluids to derive the most basic line element. We obtain completely new and different (from prior publications) fully self-gravitating configuration for this configuration by employing the hydrostatic equilibrium condition (Einstein field equations) in the radial direction. We have demonstrated through analysis (numerically) that the resulting configuration can meet necessary conditions (physically reasonable) on both surfaces (internal as well external). Moreover, different conditions (barotropic as well as non-conservative) have been test (internally). Finally, we have compared our configuration with a reference configuration (tabulated data for Sun as well as VY CMi).

While most current Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) techniques primarily concentrate on generating extensive pseudo-training data to improve performance, very few tackle the challenge of few-shot domain adaptation. This study redefines various GEC environments as distinct tasks and introduces a methodology for few-shot domain adaptation by leveraging pseudo-training data within a meta-learning framework. Specifically, we generate large-scale high-quality pseudo-training sets across multiple English dialects. Using this diverse data, we train a model capable of swiftly adapting to new, low-resource domains with minimal examples. Experiments conducted on four diverse domain settings demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances performance even when only using a handful of data samples compared to current state-of-the-art domain adaptation techniques. Additionally, an in-depth analysis of different pseudo-data strategies and the count of examples offers valuable insights. Finally, we examine the cross-lingual applicability of our approach; although not directly optimized for it, the method exhibits some capacity for fast learning and adaptation to new languages with a modest decrease in performance.

This paper examines the allocation of indivisible goods among strategic agents with additive valuation functions, operating in a non-monetary setting where a mechanism is considered valid only if it induces Pure Nash Equilibria (PNE) that are both efficient and fair. We establish that, except for dictatorial mechanisms, all other PNE-inducing mechanisms generally fail to be efficient. Specifically, we demonstrate lower bounds for deterministic mechanisms that are exponentially low in $n$ (the agent count) and for randomized mechanisms that are exponentially low in $\log n$. Conversely, we also explore positive territories by presenting a bounded randomness mechanism which is deterministic and distributes fairness guarantees. Along the lines, we show that any deterministic mechanism that is fair must have exponential lower bounds in the number of items. Finally, we examine deterministic mechanisms that are not efficient either, showing they are fair in terms of stochastic Nash equilibrium. These results indicate that there exists a deterministic mechanism that is both efficient and fair, while showing that the set of such mechanisms is non-empty. In summary, we present new lower and upper bounds for the allocation of indivisible goods among strategic agents, demonstrating the existence of deterministic mechanisms that are both efficient and fair, as well as showing the fairness of PNE under specific conditions.

The regulation of protoplanetary disk evolution relies on analyzing how accretion rates scale with star and disk attributes; however, utilizing the distribution of these relations as a constraint on evolutionary models requires accurately accounting for accretion fluctuations. A strong edge-edge coloring scheme of a graph $G$ involves edge coloring $G$ such that every vertex has incident edges within at least three different colors; the smallest number of colors needed for this is denoted as $\sigma_1(G)$. In a prior study published in the SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics (2006), it was demonstrated through counterexample that for any sufficiently large cubic bipartite graph $G$, the value $\sigma_1(G)$ equals $6$. Continuing this line, our research presents an improved counterexample valid for cubic bipartite graphs where $6 < |E(G)| \leqslant 50$, and moreover establishes the precise relationship $\sigma_1(G) = 6 + \lfloor\sqrt{|E(G)| - 18.242}\rfloor$ whenever $6 < |E(G)| \leqslant 20000$, further tightening the bound where $6 < |E(G)|$.

We apply co-evolutionary genetic algorithms to simulate player learning and adaptation in a duopoly, comparing the outcomes against standard models. The analysis examines how different adaptation mechanisms—specifically "red queen" dynamics and "mutated best response" strategies—interact within a duopolistic market. Key factors under investigation include the mutation rate and initial population diversity. The simulation demonstrates that both the mutation rate and initial population variance significantly influence whether a population converges on a symmetric Nash Equilibrium (neq). Specifically, a larger variance among initial conditions and higher mutation rates increase the likelihood of disruption, preventing the population from stabilising at the neq. Additionally, the study finds evidence to support the hypothesis derived from the "red queen" dynamics: diversity within the population tends to decrease over the lifecycle.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are now integral to many safety-critical computer vision tasks, such as automated driving and human-robot collaboration. To ensure these systems remain functional in real-world settings, it is essential to defend against hardware memory faults. Drawing on the known effectiveness of activation clipping, this study establishes a preliminary safety argument for convolutional classifier by showing that range supervision acts as a robust detector and countermeasure against specific bit-flip faults when utilizing eight-exponent floating-point representations. Additionally, we investigate new non-uniform range restriction strategies that substantially lower the likelihood of silent data corruption and uncorrectable errors. As a proof of practical application, our model demonstrates improved vehicle recognition in an end-to-end traffic classification scenario using the MIOVision dataset with ResNet-50. The quantitative results presented here can serve as a foundation for developing more sophisticated CNN safety justifications.

We propose a multilingual common semantic space grounded in distributional semantics, enabling knowledge and resource sharing by projecting vocabulary from various languages into an integrated representation space that exceeds basic pairwise word alignment. Specifically, we develop two approaches that respectively align word clusters with their local neighbor clusters and global co-occurrence clusters. Notably, the resulting multilingual common semantic space remains learnable using only monolingual data at the initiator languages, offering substantial practical advantages.

In the latter half of October 2019, widespread violence sweeping through Chile and, most severely, its capital city, Santiago, caused widespread destruction of public and commercial infrastructure. This paper introduces a novel approach to the containment problem for extended regular expressions, enhancing basic regex capabilities with intersection and complementation while handling infinite alphabets via potentially limitless character sets. Unlike traditional methods that fail to manage extended operators or such vast character collections, the proposed algorithm expresses the left-hand side of an inequality—potentially involving multiple intersections—into canonical Disjunctive Normal Form. It evaluates each term within this structure using a Brzozowski-style solver to determine truth values. Although the process involves non-trivial logic evaluation due to expression complexity, the method ultimately yields a binary result. As it avoids constructing an explicit automaton for every expression variant, it is distinguished by space-efficient resource utilization.

Precise and resilient localization represents a critical requirement for autonomous mobile entities. Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) methods utilize data from cameras and inertial units to determine position and orientation, and recent deep learning approaches to VIO have garnered significant focus by delivering pose estimates through a data-driven paradigm, eliminating the need for manually designed heuristics. Although these learning-based models typically deploy recurrent networks to integrate multimodal sensor information, such architectures often struggle with training convergence and lack sufficient efficiency. We introduce a novel learning-based VIO framework incorporating external memory-based attention, which streamlines the fusion of visual and inertial features to enhance state estimation. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) are increasingly prominent, though most models learn node embeddings within Euclidean geometry. This Euclidean approach can introduce high distortion when embedding graphs possessing hierarchical or scale-free characteristics. In response, researchers have turned to non-Euclidean geometries like the hyperbolic plane. Despite the promising results achieved by hyperbolic GCNs, existing hyperbolic graph operations strictly adhere to these geometric constraints, potentially restricting their full capability and affecting performance. We propose Lorentzian graph convolutional network (LGCN), a novel hyperbolic GCN that strictly enforces adherence to Lorentzian (hyperbolic) geometry for node embeddings. Our approach leverages the refined and computationally efficient Lorentzian versions of standard graph convolution operations—specifically Sparse, Residual, and Attention convolutions—while also introducing a newly defined Lorentzian graph attention mechanism. We identify an attention mechanism implemented via Lorentzian norms as a key innovation, offering both conceptual clarity and computational benefits compared to prior methods. Empirical results demonstrate that LGCN outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in hyperbolic geometries across three diverse tasks: transductive and inductive node classification, hierarchical classification, and link prediction, all with notably lower embedding distortions.

ViDaExpert serves as a specialized utility for the visualization and analysis of multidimensional vectorial datasets. Designed to handle "object-feature" formatted tables—controlling both numerical attributes and textual row/column labels—it integrates a suite of statistical techniques, including standard and weighted Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Elastic Maps (offering a non-linear approach to PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and multilinear regression, alongside K-Means clustering and decision-tree construction variants. Featuring an array of intuitive dialogs for configuring data point properties such as size, shape, and color, along with rapid 3D rendering capabilities, ViDa Expert functions as a powerful instrument. This enables users to generate interactive 3D scenes representing high-dimensional data tables while efficiently executing both foundational and sophisticated statistical analyses.
